key_insight: Real-world immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes varied by cancer type and performance status, with some patients surviving long after treatment discontinuation.
clinical_relevance: Performance status may help contextualize differences between routine-care survival and pivotal trial outcomes.
method: Retrospective cohort of 3,231 adults treated with ICIs across four Belgian hospitals.
Harmonized electronic health records using OMOP-CDM and natural language processing.
Evaluated survival and treatment trajectories, with descriptive trial comparisons and multivariable Cox regression.
evidence_signal: Among 568 metastatic patients who discontinued ICI without subsequent systemic therapy, median post-discontinuation survival was 21.4 months; ECOG ≥2 was associated with poorer overall survival than ECOG 0–1 (adjusted HR 2.18, 95% CI 1.82–2.60).
watch_item: Retrospective observational data and descriptive trial comparisons cannot establish causal treatment effects or explain survival differences fully.
paper_title: Comprehensive real-world utilization, treatment trajectories, and outcomes of immune checkpoint inhibitors across cancer types: the multicenter FAIR-ICI cohort
